exhibits.title: The Echoed Gaze
exhibits.text:
No caption hangs on any wall here. This chamber learns to see with no words offered to it at all — only an image, and a single stubborn demand: TWO VIEWS OF ONE THING MUST BE SEEN THE SAME.

Before the tall mirror stand two watchers cut from the same cloth. The STUDENT is given only a small torn crop of the scene — a corner, a fragment — and asked what it is. The TEACHER, in the glass, is shown the whole picture, the grand view. The student must make its answer echo the teacher's. Looking at a scrap, it must guess what the whole would say. To do that, it is forced to learn 'this small piece belongs to this kind of larger world'.

But watch the trap laid at the mirror's foot. There is a cheat that satisfies the demand perfectly: let both watchers answer the SAME dull thing for every image — one flat, constant reply. Then the two views always agree, the regret falls to nothing, and the features learned are worthless. This is COLLAPSE, and it is the whole peril of learning without labels. Everything else in this room is machinery built to refuse it.

Mark one thing about the figure in the glass: the teacher is no wiser twin trained apart. It is the student's own past self, slowed. Its form drifts toward the student's by a running average, a faint delayed echo — a stable, slowly-moving target to chase. If the reflection lurched as fast as the student moved, there would be nothing steady to aim at, and the learning would shake itself apart.

exhibits.title: Two Views, One Truth
exhibits.text:
The whole training signal is drawn from the image itself — no captions, no class names, nothing borrowed from language.

Take one image. Make two different augmented crops of it. Demand that both encode to the SAME representation. That is the entire objective: two views of one thing should be seen the same. From this alone, without a single label, the features that emerge turn out to be spatially precise and richly structured.

The danger built into that demand is COLLAPSE. The objective has a trivial, useless solution: output one constant vector for every input whatsoever. Then all views match, the regret is exactly zero, and nothing has been learned. A learner with no labels cannot be told 'that answer is wrong' by any outside authority — so preventing collapse becomes the entire design problem. The methods differ only in HOW they forbid the flat answer.

exhibits.title: Student and Teacher, One Bloodline
exhibits.text:
DINO forbids collapse by SELF-DISTILLATION — a student learning from a teacher who is really itself, delayed.

Two networks of identical architecture:

  STUDENT — trained by gradient descent, the one that actually learns. It is shown small LOCAL crops.

  TEACHER — never touched by a gradient. Its weights are an EXPONENTIAL MOVING AVERAGE (EMA) of the student's: after each step the teacher creeps a fraction of the way toward the student and no more. It is shown large GLOBAL crops.

The objective: the student's output should match the teacher's. Seeing only a fragment, the student must predict what the teacher sees taking in the whole scene. That is what forces genuine understanding — a local patch must encode enough to anticipate its global context.

Why the teacher must be an EMA and not a fresh twin: it provides a STABLE, slowly-moving target. Chase a target that jerks as fast as you move and training never settles. The slow echo is what makes the aim hold still enough to hit.

exhibits.title: The Two Restraints
exhibits.text:
The EMA teacher gives a steady target, but by itself it will not stop the flat answer. Two further restraints are laid on the TEACHER's output, and they work only as a balanced pair:

  CENTERING — subtract a running mean from the teacher's output. This stops any one dimension from swelling to dominate every answer. It SPREADS the output out.

  SHARPENING — apply a low temperature to the teacher's softmax, making its target confident and peaked. It CONCENTRATES the output.

Hold them together and see the tension: centering pushes the distribution to spread across dimensions; sharpening pulls it to a sharp point. Centering alone would drift toward a uniform, uninformative smear; sharpening alone would let the output pile onto one dimension and collapse. Balanced against each other, they keep the representation from ever falling to a constant — spread enough to be informative, peaked enough to be decisive. Neither restraint works alone; the anti-collapse lives in the pair.

exhibits.caption: The student sees a local crop and must predict the EMA teacher's answer on a global crop. Centering and sharpening, applied to the teacher, are the balanced pair that keeps the shared target from collapsing to a constant. The teacher is never trained by gradients; it only drifts slowly after the student.

exhibits.title: Three Roads Away from Collapse
exhibits.text:
DINO is one member of a whole family — two views, no labels, agree without collapsing. What separates the family is HOW each refuses the flat answer. There are three roads:

  DISTILLATION — an EMA teacher supplies a moving target. DINO walks this road; so do BYOL and V-JEPA. (The great video seer of the floor below, V-JEPA, is kin to this room — same slow-echoing teacher, but it predicts in LATENT space, never pixels.)

  REGULARIZATION — no teacher at all. Explicit loss terms force the features to spread: keep each dimension's variance up, decorrelate the dimensions, and still make the views agree.

  RECONSTRUCTION — mask out patches of the image and rebuild them (the MAE road, met in the Helm at this wing's end).

The regularization road has its own chamber already raised. Pass through the archway from this room into the CORRIDOR OF THE THREE VOWS, where VICReg forbids collapse with three explicit vows — variance, invariance, covariance — and no teacher is needed at all. DINO and VICReg are cousins solving one problem two ways: walk between them and see the whole family.

exhibits.title: Of the Gaze That Taught Itself, and Its Greater Heir
exhibits.text:
DINO — SELF-DISTILLATION WITH NO LABELS

The objective is bare: one image, two augmented crops, and the demand that both encode to the same representation. From that alone rich visual structure appears. The peril is collapse — the trivial constant answer that satisfies the demand and teaches nothing.

The cure is a student and an EMA teacher of identical architecture. The student, gradient-trained, is fed small local crops. The teacher, its weights a slow exponential moving average of the student's and never touched by a gradient, is fed large global crops. The student must make its answer on a fragment match the teacher's answer on the whole — learning that a local piece belongs to a particular kind of global scene. The EMA gives a stable, slowly-moving target; a target as fast as the student would never let training settle.

Two restraints on the teacher's output prevent collapse and only work as a pair. CENTERING subtracts a running mean, so no single dimension dominates — it spreads the output out. SHARPENING applies a low temperature to the teacher's softmax, making the target confident and peaked — it concentrates the output. Balanced, they hold the representation between a uniform smear and a collapsed spike.

WHAT DINO FEATURES ARE GOOD AT

The features come out spatially precise and semantically structured, yet with NO language grounding — nothing ever connected them to words. Most striking: the attention maps segment objects with no segmentation supervision at all; object structure simply falls out of the representation. They are strong for dense prediction (depth, segmentation), for correspondence and matching, for k-NN retrieval and linear probing — anywhere precise 'where is what' structure matters.

DINOv2 — THE GENERAL-PURPOSE EYE

DINOv2 scales the recipe up. A much larger, carefully CURATED dataset — LVD-142M — and bigger models, and crucially it combines DINO's image-level objective with iBOT's PATCH-LEVEL masked objective. The result is a general-purpose visual backbone: the go-to self-supervised encoder for dense features and spatial precision, reached for in depth, segmentation, correspondence, and robotics perception. DINOv3 scales it further still.

SIGLIP VERSUS DINOv2 — THE TWO KINDS OF SIGHT

Set the language-aligned eye beside the self-supervised one:

  SigLIP asks 'what does this image MEAN in language terms?' Its features are semantic and language-aligned — excellent for VLMs and zero-shot classification — but weaker in spatial precision, because caption supervision is image-level and never rewards pixel-precise localization.

  DINOv2 asks 'what is the visual STRUCTURE here?' Its features are spatially precise and dense and superb for geometry — but carry NO language alignment, and so offer no zero-shot classification, because nothing connects them to words.

This is not a wall but a gradient, as the Helm at the end of this wing will insist. It is also exactly why so many systems refuse to choose, and fuse both.

exhibits.title: The Student, the Echoed Teacher, and the Balance
exhibits.caption: Read the gaze in its parts. The STUDENT is fed small local crops and trained by gradient descent; the TEACHER is fed large global crops and is never trained directly — its weights are an exponential moving average of the student's, a slow echo. The student's task is to make its output on a fragment match the teacher's output on the whole. On the teacher's side sit the two balanced restraints: CENTERING subtracts a running mean to spread the answer across dimensions, and SHARPENING applies a low-temperature softmax to peak it up — together they refuse collapse. The small inset contrasts a COLLAPSED representation (every input crushed to nearly one point, useless) against a HEALTHY one (features spread across the space) — the difference the two restraints buy.
